questions.question: In a right triangle, the side opposite angle θ is 3 and the hypotenuse is 5. Then sin θ equals:
questions.rationale: Sine is opposite over hypotenuse, so sin θ = 3/5; 4/5 would be the cosine and 5/3 the cosecant.

questions.question: The value of cos 60° is:
questions.rationale: From the standard angles table, cos 60° = 1/2 (and sin 60° = √3/2).

questions.question: The value of tan 45° is:
questions.rationale: sin 45° = cos 45°, so their ratio tan 45° = 1 — the only standard angle where opposite and adjacent are equal.

questions.question: A 10 m ladder leans against a wall at 60° to the ground. The height it reaches is:
questions.rationale: height = 10 × sin 60° = 10 × (√3/2) = 5√3 ≈ 8.66 m; the ladder itself is the hypotenuse.

questions.question: If sin θ = 5/13 with θ acute, then cos θ equals:
questions.rationale: cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ = 1 − 25/169 = 144/169, so cos θ = 12/13 — the 5-12-13 triangle.

questions.question: For every angle θ, sin²θ + cos²θ equals:
questions.rationale: This is the Pythagorean identity: the two squared ratios partition the hypotenuse, so they always sum to 1.

questions.question: sin 20° is equal to:
questions.rationale: Complementary angles swap sine and cosine: sin θ = cos(90° − θ), and 20° + 70° = 90°.

questions.question: A pole casts a 20 m shadow when the sun's elevation is 30°. The pole's height is:
questions.rationale: height = shadow × tan 30° = 20 × (1/√3) = 20/√3 ≈ 11.55 m; the shadow is the adjacent side.

questions.question: The reciprocal ratio sec θ is defined as:
questions.rationale: Secant is the reciprocal of cosine: sec θ = 1/cos θ; 1/sin θ is cosecant and 1/tan θ is cotangent.

questions.question: From two points 40 m apart on a road, a tower's elevations are 60° and 30°. The tower's height is:
questions.rationale: Solving tan 60° = h/x and tan 30° = h/(x + 40) together gives h(√3 − 1/√3) = 40, so h = 20√3 ≈ 34.6 m.
